channel.title: The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (occrp.org)

item.title: Former Mayor Arrested in Georgia Over Hotel Permit Issued to Wife’s Company
item.description: Georgia arrested a former mayor for allegedly abusing his post when issuing a building permit to the company of his wife. The arrest follows an investigation by OCCRP and iFact that detailed a conflict of interest and construction violations.

item.title: Haitian Police Kill 16 Suspected Gang Members in Anti-Gang Sweep
item.description: Gang violence has displaced over 1.4 million people in Haiti, more than half of whom are children facing extreme forms of exploitation, the UN warned.

item.title: Hungary to Veto New EU Russia Sanctions Over Druzhba Oil Transit
item.description: Hungary says it will block the EU’s planned 20th sanctions package — and other Ukraine-related decisions requiring unanimity — until oil flows to Hungary and Slovakia resume through the Druzhba pipeline, which has been down since late January after reported Russian strikes in western Ukraine.

item.title: Eurojust-Backed Operation Takes Down Ukrainian Scam Call Center
item.description: The Eurojust operation mirrors UN concerns over coerced labor in scam call centers, highlighting the intersection of financial crime and human rights abuses.

item.title: Belarusian Companies Supply Chain Behind Russian Bomb Attacks
item.description: Customs data shows shipments of key components to manufacturers linked to deadly glide-bomb strikes.

item.title: Ukraine Detains Officer Over Alleged Draft-Evasion Bribe Scheme
item.description: Ukraine Detains Officer Over Alleged Draft-Evasion Bribe Scheme

item.title: Report and Survive: Ukraine’s Young Journalists Investigate Through the War’s Most Brutal Winter
item.description: Russia’s attacks on energy infrastructure, waged during the coldest winter in memory, have pushed Ukrainians to their limits. But in freezing offices and darkened apartments, a new generation of investigative journalists is still at work.

item.title: Europe Files First War Crimes Charges Four Years After Full-Scale Invasion of Ukraine
item.description: European and Ukrainian authorities have filed the first charges in connection with crimes committed during Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, with trial proceedings now under way. UN experts warn the conflict continues to fuel human rights abuses inside occupied areas and within Russia.

item.title: Rights Watchdog Sounds Alarm over Arbitrary Arrests in Iran
item.description: From the massacres in early January to the ongoing use of secret trials, Iranian authorities’ systematic impunity has sustained the brutal violent clampdown on protesters.

item.title: UK Sanctions Georgian TV Channels Over Ukraine Disinformation
item.description: On the fourth anniversary of Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the U.K. has sanctioned Georgian channels Imedi TV and PosTV for allegedly spreading false information about Ukraine and its leadership.
